the time complexities of the best known algorithms for the problem of order-preserving pattern-matching in ternary relations are O(nm) and O(n + m log m), where n and m are the lengths of the two strings.
order-preserving matching can be solved in $$O(n+m\log m)$$ time, where n and m are the lengths of the input strings.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we extend Kim et al.’s work to ternary order relation, and prove the correctness of the extended representations.
the time complexities of the order-preserving matching problem for ternary order relations are the same with those of binary ones.

the time complexity of order-preserving string matching is $$O\left( {m\log n+n}\right)$$ in binary order relations, and $$O\left({m\log n}\right)$$ or $$O\left(m\log m\right)$$ in ternary order relation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we can apply the existing algorithms for order-preserving matching on binary order relations to the ternary order relations without any modifications.
the order-preserving matching problem is not affected by the type of order relations, which can be either binary or ternary.
